title: "Changelog"
---

# v520.3.0 - UNRELEASED

## Added
- Compositor node groups under a new `Compositor` catalog: `Illustrate` (flat, illustrative shading from the AO or Shadow pass or a `Cone Shadow`, with outlines and a flat background), `Depth Outline` and `Outline` (outlines from the Depth pass, by a Sobel filter or Goodsell's *Illustrate* contour method, optionally with lines from the Normal pass, that survive transparent backgrounds), and `Value to Mask` and `Mask Pixels` for masking by an AOV pass. `canvas.compositor.illustrate()` enables the passes and inserts the composite in one call; `canvas.add_aov()` and `mn.material.add_aov()` set up AOV passes; `shadow` joins the render passes.
- Parts of David Goodsell's *Illustrate* renderer as compositor node groups (reference in `docs/dev/illustrate-pipeline.md`): `Cone Shadow` (conical soft shadow from the Depth pass, 32 samples), `ID Outline` (chain and residue outlines from `chain_id`/`res_id` AOVs) and `Composite Depth Fog`. `canvas.compositor.illustrate(shading="cone")` shades with the cone shadow; meant for the `Flat` material.
- Added the `Segment ID` attribute input node, which reads the integer `segid` attribute from the points. [#1216](https://github.com/BradyAJohnston/MolecularNodes/issues/1216)
- Added a general handler that triggers after nodes are added to the tree in the GUI. Sets the default material of style nodes and generates data objects for biological assemblies. [#1191](https://github.com/BradyAJohnston/MolecularNodes/pull/1191)
- `Charge` attribute input node under Attributes, reading the `charge` attribute with a fallback of `0.0`. [#1216](https://github.com/BradyAJohnston/MolecularNodes/issues/1216)
- `Ease Value` and `Stagger Value` nodes under Animate: Penner easing curves (In / Out / In Out) for any 0..1 value or field, and a per-point stagger that gives each ID its own equal-length 0..1 transition.
- `Symmetry Cubic` node under Ensemble: builds tetrahedral (12), octahedral (24) or icosahedral (60) assemblies from one copy, with an `Orientation` to match a deposited structure.
- `Best View` and `Orient to Best View` nodes under Geometry: find the direction from which the most selected atoms can be seen past a style's meshes, and rotate the geometry so the camera looks from there. For trajectories, views can ease with a half-life, favour the view on screen (`Stickiness`) and hold it until a better one gains a margin (`Hysteresis`). `Camera Transform` gives the equivalent camera pose, to move a camera with a Geometry Attribute constraint and leave the geometry in place. [#1171](https://github.com/BradyAJohnston/MolecularNodes/issues/1171)
- `Canvas.look_at(viewpoint=...)` accepts `"pca"`, `"unobstructed"`, `"visible_area"`, `"raycast"` and `"entropy"` to choose the camera direction from the target, with `occluders` for what could hide it. Experimental. [#1171](https://github.com/BradyAJohnston/MolecularNodes/issues/1171)
- Hydrogen bonds: `mol.calculations.hbonds()` adds the `hbonds` calculation, computing hydrogen bonds with MDAnalysis `HydrogenBondAnalysis` as edges on a data object rather than as an attribute, and the new `Style HBonds` node draws them as dashed cylinders following the atom positions. Its distance and angle cutoffs are properties, adjustable in its settings in the Attributes panel. It is listed there as an Object, added from its add menu, and set up when a `Style HBonds` node is added in the GUI.
- `Find HBonds` node: finds hydrogen bonds in the node tree, with the same cutoffs as MDAnalysis, giving each hydrogen's acceptor as a field. `Style HBonds` can use it with `Source` set to `Find HBonds` instead of a data object.
- `Symmetry Helical` takes an `Axial Symmetry` input for filaments with Cn symmetry about the helix axis, such as amyloid built from two protofilaments.
- `Color Sample Grid` node under Color: colors points by sampling a float grid from a volume object, such as an APBS electrostatic potential (`.dx`) on a molecular surface, with a diverging A / Intermediate / B color range between `Min` and `Max`. Its `Value` output gives the sampled value. `Molecule.add_style(color=density)` accepts a density entity and colors the style's output this way. A density can be sampled while it is styled: its grid is kept in the bundle of the styled output (see `Import Volume`).
- An Electrostatics guide in the API docs colours a barnase-barstar surface (PDB 1BRS) by its APBS potential. The potential ships as `tests/data/1brs_AD_apbs.dx.gz`, made by `docs/dev/apbs_1brs.py`.
- Densities are imported in their node tree: the object is an empty mesh, and each branch of the tree starts with a new `Import Volume` node that reads the converted `.vdb` with Blender's `Import VDB` node, instead of the object being a volume made by an import operator. [#893](https://github.com/BradyAJohnston/MolecularNodes/issues/893) `Grids.load()` takes a list of files to load as one density, played one file per frame from `frame_start` (or picked with the node's `Index`), for animated densities. [#1100](https://github.com/BradyAJohnston/MolecularNodes/issues/1100) `Import Volume` keeps its grid in the bundle of its output as `MN Grid <Name>`, which density styles pass on, so `Color Sample Grid` can sample several named grids of one styled density. `Grids.import_volume()` gives the node set up for a density's files. Density trees have no input geometry: `density.tree.reset()` yields `(None, join)`.
- Fetch small molecules from PubChem by CID or name: `mn.Molecule.fetch("aspirin", database="pubchem")` downloads the 3D conformer as SDF, and the import panel has a `Fetch from PubChem` button.
- `Align Molecules` operator (viewport right-click menu) and `Molecule.align_to()`: superimpose the selected molecules onto the active one by setting their object transforms. Residues are paired by sequence alignment (biotite's `superimpose_homologs`) or, for remote homologs, by structure (`superimpose_structural_homologs`), so the sequences don't need to match. The operator opens a dialog listing each molecule's chains, where optional selections pick the chains to fit on. When the two sides have different numbers of chains (e.g. a Fab's heavy and light chains against a single-chain scFv), each is joined into one chain and aligned as a whole.
- `mn.Canvas()` takes `view_transform=` and `background=`, e.g. `mn.Canvas(view_transform="Standard", background=(1, 1, 1, 1))`; left out, the preset's settings are kept.
- Calculations in `Molecule.calculations` can be set to not update on frame changes (`calculations.add(name, func, updating=False)`, `calculations.set_updating(name, ...)` and a toggle in the Attributes list), keeping their values from when they last ran. A trajectory whose files have no secondary structure gets DSSP as the `sec_struct` calculation on load, run on the first frame and not updating. DSSP is set up again from its saved settings after a file is reopened, where it previously stopped updating.
- Trajectory frames with velocities or forces (such as frames of `.trr` files) store them as the `velocity` and `force` point attributes, interpolated and averaged between frames like positions. Frames without them keep the values last stored. `velocity` is scaled by the world scale; `force` keeps MDAnalysis units of kJ/(mol·Å). Other per-atom values MDAnalysis reads for each frame are stored too: `b_factor` and `occupancy` for each model of a multi-model `.pdb` file (and of a multi-model `.pdb`, `.cif` or `.bcif` file loaded on its own, when they differ between models), LAMMPS dump `additional_columns` (`q` as `charge`) and `.tng` `additional_blocks`, with a `ts_` prefix for any other name that would overwrite a built-in attribute. A new Attributes panel, after the Trajectory panel, lists the attributes updated on each frame, from the trajectory, selections and calculations, with an icon for the source of each (also `Molecule.frame_attributes`) and buttons to show only one source. It replaces the separate Selections list, which was only in the Properties editor: selections are added from the list's add menu, and the selected selection's string and settings show below the list. `Bake Frames to Collection` (`Molecule.frames_to_collection()`) stores these attributes on each baked frame object as well as positions. A new `Force` node reads the `force` attribute, like the `Velocity` node does for `velocity`.

## Changed
- DSSP moved from `mol.dssp` to `mol.calculations.dssp(selection=None, updating=None)`, which sets it up if needed, changes only the settings given and returns the `DSSPCalculation` (previously `DSSPManager`) with the same `show_*`, `set_selection` and `compute_frame` methods. `mol.dssp.init()` becomes `mol.calculations.dssp(updating=True)`. The DSSP panel is removed: its settings show when `sec_struct` is selected in the Attributes list. DSSP is added from the Attributes list's add menu, and the X on a selection or calculation in the list removes it (a removed calculation's attribute keeps its last values).
- The `Ambient Occlusion` material is always opaque and no longer fades with `Fade Geometry`, because ambient occlusion does not work alongside a Transparent BSDF. Its default exponent is now 1.5, for slightly lighter crevices.
- The `Flat` material renders without outlines by default; `Flat(outline=True)` adds them. The `Flat Outline` material is renamed `Fresnel Outline`.
- `Animate Action` now takes float `Start` and `Length`, can run on scene seconds, frames or a linked value, and has built-in `Stagger` and `Easing` options.
- The `oxDNA Style Ribbon` node is renamed `oxDNA Style Classic`. Its inputs are now in Å, its defaults match other oxDNA visualisers, `Ball Radius` no longer changes the backbone radius, base stems and bases share one rotation and end at the centre of the base, a `Stem Geometry` input takes custom stem geometry, backbone ends are filled, and `End Overhang` extends strand ends for the `Curve` backbone. [#1213](https://github.com/BradyAJohnston/MolecularNodes/pull/1213)
- Importing structures is 3-5x faster. Per-atom attributes such as `is_backbone` and `is_peptide` test each unique residue or atom name once instead of every atom, and the preset materials read the node asset library once instead of once per node group.
- Adding a style is 25-50% faster. The node asset library ships uncompressed, which makes each read of it ~40% faster, and `add_style` links the node groups it needs (style, color scheme, assembly) in one read instead of one read each. The installed extension is ~27 MB larger; saved `.blend` files are unchanged.
- `Outline Mask`, and the outlines of the `Flat` material, keep the same on-screen width at any camera focal length. Outlines previously grew with focal length and were far too thick on telephoto lenses. The width at the default 50 mm lens is unchanged.
- Trajectory periodic correction (`correct_periodic`) works with triclinic boxes, such as rhombic dodecahedra and hexagonal cells, as well as orthorhombic ones, using MDAnalysis's minimum image convention (`MDAnalysis.lib.distances.minimize_vectors`). Interpolation uses the box of the current frame and averaging the box of the averaged frame. Frames with no box, or the `1 1 1 90 90 90` placeholder box, are not corrected.
- `Density Style ISO Surface` is simplified: its `Negative Color` and `Positive Color` inputs are renamed `Negative` and `Positive`, a `Process Grid` closure can modify the grid before it is meshed, and the `Visible`, contour and slice inputs are removed. The new `Mesh Contours` node turns the edges of a mesh, such as an ISO surface, into tubes.
- The Reload operator (`mn.session_reload_item`) relinks any entity object to the session from its recorded source files or PDB code, replacing `mn.reload_trajectory`. [#1244](https://github.com/BradyAJohnston/MolecularNodes/pull/1244)

## Fixed
- `.cif` files from Phenix (such as `phenix.real_space_refine` output) now import. Biotite failed on their indented `loop_` tags and on the atom-free restraint blocks (`data_link_SS`) appended after the model. A `.cif` with several structures in separate data blocks imports as one Molecule per block; from a script, `Molecule.load(path, data_block=...)` chooses the block.
- Importing a CellPack model whose name is already taken no longer adds its molecules to the earlier import's instance collection and node tree.
- The `atom_types` attribute of structure files (`.pdb`, `.cif`, `.bcif`, `.sdf`, `.mol`) comes from each atom's element instead of being guessed by MDAnalysis from its atom name. Calcium ions (atom name `CA`) are no longer typed as carbon, and `.sdf` / `.mol` files, which have no atom names, no longer give every atom the same type. Loading is also slightly faster.
- oxDNA trajectories are restored when reopening a saved `.blend` file, instead of the `.top` topology being read with Amber's parser and failing. [#1253](https://github.com/BradyAJohnston/MolecularNodes/issues/1253)
- An entity that fails to restore when reopening a `.blend` file (for example because its trajectory file was moved) no longer stops every other entity in the file from restoring. A warning names the entity and points to Reload to relink it. Sessions saved with this version load in older versions as an empty session.
- The oxDNA style node colours every strand with the strand colours, instead of only strands whose `chain_id` modulo 4 is non-zero, and the backbone offset uses the correct cross product so the major and minor grooves are no longer swapped. [#1213](https://github.com/BradyAJohnston/MolecularNodes/pull/1213)
- Styles keep the atoms they were given in the `MN/Atoms` bundle of their output, so `Get Geometry Atoms` (and add-ons reading an evaluated molecule) can still find the atoms after a style is applied, and styles stack: each joins its result to the earlier styles' geometry. `Evaluate on Atoms` `Result` is now `Atoms` (default, operate on the geometry directly) or `Representation` (used by styles), replacing `Geometry` / `Bundle`.
- Styles use the bonds found by `Find Bonds` again. `Evaluate on Atoms` no longer attaches the stored `MN/Atoms` bundle when it returns geometry, so styles read the new geometry instead of the stored atoms. [#1231](https://github.com/BradyAJohnston/MolecularNodes/issues/1231)
- `Build Elastic Network` builds networks again, with van der Waals radii passed to its `Plexus` input. Simulating the network is still not fully working. [#1229](https://github.com/BradyAJohnston/MolecularNodes/issues/1229)
- Import operators give clearer error messages for empty or missing file paths. [#1242](https://github.com/BradyAJohnston/MolecularNodes/pull/1242)
- `Color to OKLab` and `OKLab to Color` now use Ottosson's linear-sRGB to LMS matrix instead of the CIE-XYZ one, so OKLab lightness, chroma and hue match the reference values and pure blue is no longer clipped to black on the round trip. Nodes built on them (`Color OKLab Mix`, `Color OKLab Offset`, `OKLab Offset LCh`, the LCh conversions) change appearance slightly.
- `is_alpha_carbon` and `is_backbone` only flag atoms in amino acid and nucleotide residues. Calcium ions (atom name `CA`) are no longer alpha carbons, and ligands such as ATP, SAM or phosphate no longer count as backbone. Modified residues such as HIC are now `is_peptide` for every format. [#1256](https://github.com/BradyAJohnston/MolecularNodes/issues/1256)
- Biological assemblies are built from `.pdb` files, including files with more than one `BIOMOLECULE` (such as 4INS). Previously `.pdb` assemblies were never built, and files with several assemblies reported none. Assembly parsing failures now log a warning instead of looking like a file without assemblies. [#1257](https://github.com/BradyAJohnston/MolecularNodes/issues/1257) [#1258](https://github.com/BradyAJohnston/MolecularNodes/issues/1258) [#1259](https://github.com/BradyAJohnston/MolecularNodes/issues/1259)
- `Simulate Elastic Network` stored twice the mass instead of the inverse mass, and the XPBD edge solver read the partner point's inverse mass at the edge index rather than the partner's point index, so constraint corrections were weighted wrongly and the mass-weighted centre drifted.
- Density grids with non-orthogonal or rotated axes are placed correctly. A `.dx` file's full `delta` matrix and an MRC/CCP4 map's cell angles now give the voxel axes, written to the `.vdb` as a full affine transform; previously only the axis lengths were used, so sheared grids such as monoclinic or hexagonal crystallographic maps came out misaligned with their structures. MRC/CCP4 maps with non-90° cells also honour their axis order (`mapc`/`mapr`/`maps`) and start indices. Orthogonal grids are written as before.
- `Density Style ISO Surface` no longer clamps `Threshold` to 0-1, so electrostatic potentials, orbitals and other grids outside that range can be contoured. It meshes at +|Threshold| and -|Threshold|, and the surface of the negative lobe now has outward-facing normals instead of inward ones.
- Density grids with 64-bit float values, which includes every `.dx` file, are stored as 32-bit float grids so Blender's grid nodes (`Get Named Grid`, `Sample Grid`) can read them; they ignore double-precision grids. Previously converted `.vdb` files are converted again on load.

# v520.2.0 - 2026-09-18

## Added
- `Color matplotlib` node: colour a 0 to 1 value with matplotlib's colormaps, grouped by category, with a reverse toggle.
- `Fade Geometry` node, which fades geometry in and out by multiplying the alpha of its `Color` attribute on the point and instance domains. The `Ambient Occlusion` material now reads that alpha, so fading works with it as well as with `Default` and `Squishy`. [#1255](https://github.com/BradyAJohnston/MolecularNodes/pull/1255)
- Added the `Segment ID` attribute input node, which reads the integer `segid` attribute from the points. [#1216](https://github.com/BradyAJohnston/MolecularNodes/issues/1216)
- `Charge` attribute input node under Attributes, reading the `charge` attribute with a fallback of `0.0`. [#1216](https://github.com/BradyAJohnston/MolecularNodes/issues/1216)
- DSSP takes a selection string (`dssp.init(selection=...)`, default `"protein"`, and a field in the trajectory panel), so termini or non-standard residues missing the required N, CA, C and O atoms can be excluded. Protein residues outside the selection are drawn as loops. [#1217](https://github.com/BradyAJohnston/MolecularNodes/issues/1217)

## Changed
- Fixed the spelling of the `Evaluate While Planar` and `Geometry to Planar` nodes (previously `Evluate While Planar` and `Geoemtry to Planar`). Scripts using `mg.EvluateWhilePlanar` or `mg.GeoemtryToPlanar` need the new `mg.EvaluateWhilePlanar` and `mg.GeometryToPlanar` names. [#1255](https://github.com/BradyAJohnston/MolecularNodes/pull/1255)
- The `lipophobicity` attribute is no longer stored on import, and partial charges are no longer looked up from the residue and atom name. Both lookups will return as nodes instead. [#1228](https://github.com/BradyAJohnston/MolecularNodes/issues/1228)

## Fixed
- The `charge` attribute is now the charge read from the file or topology (the PDB charge column, mmCIF `pdbx_formal_charge`, which mmCIF and BinaryCIF files now read, or a simulation topology's charges) instead of a partial charge looked up from the residue and atom name that masked it. It is only stored when the file or topology provides charges; the `Charge` node reads `0.0` otherwise. [#1221](https://github.com/BradyAJohnston/MolecularNodes/issues/1221)
- Manual frame management (`Update with Scene` off) now uses the same subframes, interpolation, averaging and periodic correction as scene playback, so the manual frame can be keyframed with interpolation between trajectory frames. The offset still only applies to scene playback. [#1218](https://github.com/BradyAJohnston/MolecularNodes/issues/1218)
- Importing with the Spheres style through the GUI always uses a `Point` cloud again, regardless of the render engine, so large systems stay interactive on import. The engine-dependent `Instance` default from #1172 still applies to `Molecule.add_style()` from the Python API. [#1220](https://github.com/BradyAJohnston/MolecularNodes/issues/1220)

## Added
- Added a general handler that triggers after nodes are added to the tree in the GUI. Sets the default material of style nodes and generates data objects for biological assemblies. [#1191](https://github.com/BradyAJohnston/MolecularNodes/pull/1191)

# v520.0.1 - 2026-09-06

## Fixed
- Text printing in a jupyter notebook crashed rendering [#1185](https://github.com/BradyAJohnston/MolecularNodes/pull/1185)

# v520.0.0 - 2026-09-05

## Added
- On using the import operators, the camera and viewport end clipping distance is increased to 10000 from 100 so users aren't confused when importing larger structures and systems #1150
- `Molecule.add_style()` accepts a callable for `style`, `selection` and `color`. The callable is evaluated inside the node tree context, so it can build any nodes from `molecularnodes.nodes.geometry` without having to write out a whole node tree:

  ```python
  mol.add_style("cartoon", color=lambda: g.ColorSecondaryStructure())
  mol.add_style("sticks", selection=lambda: g.IsPeptide() & g.IsSideChain())
  mol.add_style(lambda: g.StyleSpheres(sphere="Instance", quality=4))
  ```

  A callable `style` defines the style node itself, so `selection`, `material` and style keyword arguments cannot be passed alongside it - passing them raises a `TypeError` rather than silently dropping them.
- `SelectionManager.node()` returns a `Named Attribute` node for a selection, creating the selection if it does not already exist. This is the bridge between selections and the node tree API, and is how an MDAnalysis selection phrase is used inside a callable style:

  ```python
  mol.add_style(lambda: g.StyleSpheres(selection=mol.selections.node("not protein")))
  ```

  Existing selections are reused - matched on the selection string together with the `updating` and `periodic` flags, or on `name` - so repeated calls do not pile up duplicate selections and mesh attributes.
- `SelectionManager.find()` looks up an existing selection by the selection string that created it, where `get()` looks a selection up by its name.
- `Canvas.look_at()` takes a `margin`, the fraction of the frame to leave empty around the subject. It defaults to `0.05`, so renders get a little breathing room rather than the subject sitting against the edge of the frame. Set it to `0` to fit the subject exactly, or go negative to crop in past its edges. #1170
- `molecularnodes.framing` solves camera framing on a set of positions. `fit_camera_to_points()` is the exact solve used by `look_at()`, with `fit_orthographic_to_points()` for orthographic cameras and `enclosing_sphere()` for framing that does not change with viewing angle. It is plain numpy, with no dependency on Blender. #1170

## Changed
- `add_style(color=...)` now validates its argument. A string must be a known keyword (`"common"`, `"default"`, `"plddt"`) or the name of an existing *colour* attribute on the molecule. Anything else raises a `UserWarning` and adds no colour, rather than silently rendering the geometry black. This includes names of attributes that exist but are not colours, such as `"b_factor"` or `"lipophobicity"`.
- `add_style(style=...)` is validated against the styles that can actually be dispatched, and the error lists them.
- `add_style("spheres")` picks its `sphere` to suit the render engine. Point clouds are only ray-traced by Cycles, so under EEVEE the spheres came out as octahedra - invisible at whole-protein zoom and glaring on a close-up. EEVEE now gets `"Instance"`, Cycles keeps `"Point"`, and passing `sphere` yourself always wins. The engine is read when the style is added, so switching engines afterwards does not revisit it. #1172
- **Breaking**: `Canvas.scene_reset()` is renamed `Canvas.load_preset()`, which is what it does - it loads a whole preset scene, its lighting, camera, world shader and render settings included. The `keep_settings` argument is gone, and `engine` now defaults to the engine the preset defines rather than forcing EEVEE. #1169
- Creating a `Canvas` no longer wipes the scene. A `template` given explicitly is always loaded, but left out the "Molecular Nodes" preset is only loaded into a scene with no molecules in it. A first `mn.Canvas()` still gets the studio lighting, while re-running the same cell - which marimo does on its own - binds to the scene and leaves the work in it alone. Previously it destroyed every molecule in the scene with no warning. Pass `template=None` to bind without loading anything. #1169
- **Breaking**: `Canvas.look_at()` accepts any number of positions, where it previously expected the 8 vertices of a bounding box. `get_view()` returns the positions making up a view rather than 8 bounding-box corners - still a `list[tuple]`, so views combine with `+` as before. `blender.utils.get_bounding_box()`, `look_at_object()` and `look_at_bbox()` are gone. #1170
- `Canvas.look_at()` frames the geometry an entity *renders* rather than the entity's bounds, so styling one chain of four frames that chain. Every component of the evaluated geometry is taken into account - a style can output a mesh, a point cloud and instances at once, and an object only ever exposes one of them through its `data`. Point clouds are grown by their radius and instances by the bounds of what they instance, so spheres are framed by their surface rather than their centres. #1170
- `Canvas.clear()` empties the scene of content rather than removing only Molecular Nodes entities. The camera, lights, render settings, world shader and compositor are kept, so the canvas is left ready to render whatever is added next, and only the canvas's own scene is touched. #1169

## Fixed
- `add_style()` raised a bare `KeyError` for style names that were accepted by validation but had no corresponding style node - `"vdw"`, `"atoms"`, `"sphere"` and `"ball+stick"` among them. These now raise a `ValueError` naming the supported styles.
- Saving a `.blend` silently lost the entire session if any entity's object had been deleted, from the outliner or otherwise. The save handler raised before writing the `.MNSession` file while the `.blend` itself saved normally, so every other molecule and trajectory in the file lost its state on reload. #1169
- Opening a second `.blend` left the previous file's entities in the session, where they raised a `LinkedObjectError` on any access. #1169
- `MNSession.remove()` raised a `LinkedObjectError` when the object behind an entity had already been deleted. The entity is now dropped either way, so removing is always safe to call - and a single stale entity can no longer abort a whole `Canvas.clear()`. #1169
- `Canvas.look_at()` pulled the camera back further than the subject needed, by a different amount from each direction. It built a mesh from the 8 corners of an axis-aligned bounding box and handed that to Blender's `camera_to_view_selected` operator; an axis-aligned box projects larger than the points inside it, and by an amount that changes with the viewing angle. Framing is now solved directly on the positions, so it is exact and consistent from any direction. #1170
- `Canvas.look_at()` silently emptied the frame when given more than 8 positions. It was annotated `list[tuple]` with no check on how many, and anything but a bounding box left the subject a few pixels wide in the middle of an empty frame. #1170
- `get_view()` read `bound_box` before the depsgraph had caught up, so what it returned depended on whether anything had happened to trigger an evaluation - a molecule read straight after `add_style()` reported the bounds of its atoms rather than of the style built from them. It also mixed spaces, returning object-local bounds without a selection and world-space ones with. Both are now world-space positions read from evaluated geometry. #1170
- `Canvas.clear()` leaked data-blocks. A molecule left behind over a hundred of them - its mesh, material and the node groups backing its styles - which accumulated on every load-and-clear cycle, as only a recursive purge collects node groups hanging off an object's modifier tree. #1169
